sentences.text: This ancient shark featured a unique skull joint connecting the upper jaw to the braincase, along with dorsal fins edged by smooth spines.
The largest known individual reached a length of approximately 1.63 meters.
The type species Protospinax annectans was discovered in the Solnhofen limestones of southern Bavaria.
Additional specimens found at Harvard University in the 1990s were previously misidentified as Squatina and Heterodontus.
Researchers suggest Protospinax was a benthopelagic shark that fed on various invertebrates with thin to hard shells, measuring between 1 and 1.6 meters.
A 2023 study classified Protospinax as a squalomorph shark, though its exact position within the group remains tentative due to a lack of unambiguous traits.
Protospinax was formerly classified in the order Squaliformes but was reclassified into its own order because that classification was paraphyletic.
Protospinax is considered a clade more closely related to sawsharks (Pristiophoriformes) and angelsharks (Squatiniformes).
Protospinax lived during the Middle to Late Jurassic in Europe and Russia.
The animal existed from the Toarcian to the Maastrichtian, spanning 184.2 to 66 million years ago.
In 2025, Begat and colleagues proposed moving three nominal species previously assigned to Protospinax into new genera.

Researchers suggest the Early Jurassic record likely represents an indeterminate Protospinax species, and only the Valanginian record from France can be reliably assigned to the genus among Early Cretaceous records.
